lesson_title: The Axis That Lies: How Graphs Fool Your Eyes
hook_text: This graph is 100% true data — and it's lying to you. Spot the trick in 5 seconds.
clip_script: A graph compares February's 300 units with July's 560 — but its number axis starts at 250 instead of nought. What is left of February above 250? A stump of 50. Of July? A tower of 310. The tower stands six times the stump, and your eye screams that winter usage exploded. The real numbers say July is not even double February. The lie lives in the missing bottom of the picture — the part where both months stood equal was cut off, so only the difference got drawn. It is a passport photo cropped to the frown. Your defence takes five seconds: look where the axis starts. If it is not nought, read the actual values and redo the comparison yourself.
visual_style: A bar chart dramatically cropped by scissors at 250, bars morphing from a shocking 6-to-1 ratio to the honest side-by-side truth as the axis zooms back to zero.
pacing: Shock reveal first, slow-motion mechanism, snappy five-second defence at the end.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to turn any graph into money decisions you can defend.
